summary: Both baseline RAWs are eligible for cleanup but the typical photo does not exercise hot-pixel repair.
evidence: Read-only production sensor helpers at ×2.3: IMG_7723.CR3 (6024×4020) had 173490 tamed and zero hot repairs; DSC00636.ARW (8660×5784) had 234541 tamed and two hot repairs. Four-phase fits succeeded on both. Both files exist under Photos/HDR Test Images.
proposed_fix: Keep typical and large, no override. ON {remove_hot_pixels:true,even_out_specks:true,speck_threshold:2.3}; OFF {remove_hot_pixels:false,even_out_specks:false,speck_threshold:2.3}. Add own #raw-even-out-specks and #raw-remove-hot-pixels clicks beside the threshold drag. Do not require a visible Fit delta for a hot-pixel-only step.
check: After blocked ON/OFF and prime, record raw_pixel_cleanup repaired/tamed, screen signature and developed-source diff; Fit visibility remains unverified.

summary: Auto lens coverage requires a known matching photo and an active distortion operation.
evidence: Read-only production _lens_modifier matched _DSC7970.ARW to Sony ILCE-7RM3 / Sigma 65mm F2 DG DN | Contemporary 020; four real coordinate rows differ with distortion OFF. Calibration includes distortion and TCA, not vignette. Historical Canon IMG_0790 match now returned no unique match in this checkout; both files are present.
proposed_fix: Override raw.lens with _DSC7970.ARW, Fit. ON {mode:'auto',distortion:true,chromatic_aberration:true,vignetting:true}; OFF {mode:'off',distortion:true,chromatic_aberration:true,vignetting:true}. Keep native distortion click plus Apply and add a Mode Off plus Apply own step if practical. Do not claim calibrated vignette coverage.
check: Assert exact resolved lens record and active coordinate correction, then compare settled screen/source signatures. Record change-to-Apply separately from Apply-to-picture.

summary: Highlight reconstruction needs a verified clipped-channel input rather than the default photo aliases.
evidence: IMG_3129.CR2 is present and the existing edge-colour-raw.js driver uses it. Read-only production opposed reconstruction at .96 found 18122/26117/1311 clipped CFA sites and changed 12458 green sites.
proposed_fix: Override raw.highlights with IMG_3129.CR2, Fit. ON {enabled:true,method:'opposed_color_v1',clipping_threshold:0.96,edge_colour_expand_percent:0.5}; OFF same fields, enabled:false. Keep native threshold and eye. Run a separate Edge colour variant on the same file (ON method edge_colour_v1, threshold .96, Expand .5; OFF bypass) if time allows, recording the GPU/CPU route.
check: Confirm clipping plus changed sensor sites and distinct settled signatures; for Edge record backend route and clipped fraction. No GPU/Electron verification in Phase 2.

summary: A RAW change made while editing SDR unexpectedly returns the viewer to HDR.
evidence: openStagedDesktopSource passes replaceSessionId and preserves the same session ID/zoom, but activateDesktopSession unconditionally sets currentView to hdr and hardcodes the initial draw, CPU fallback and Denoise recalculation to HDR. setRaw in the audit driver reapplies only zoom, so --lane sdr RAW rows may probe the wrong lane or fail.
proposed_fix: Preserve the active lane for same-session RAW re-development and pass that lane through first draw, fallback and Denoise; leave new opens at HDR. Driver should assert the requested lane after every seed/restore.
check: On a disposable RAW in SDR, toggle Highlight Reconstruction and verify the first exact frame and controls remain in SDR; repeat HDR and confirm unchanged output per lane.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction. Also affects raw.cleanup and raw.lens.

summary: Every lens-only re-development repeats the unchanged RAW decode, cleanup, highlight reconstruction and colour conversion.
evidence: The import job releases derived state and calls prepare_session → load_image → decode_raw, and _decode_raw always calls its inspect/decode/correct stages; the existing cleanup cache replays repairs but does not retain pre-lens developed RGB. November 22 prior equipped Sony replay attributed 10.534 s to pre-Lensfun RAW work at 78% with Micro Grain on, a different condition from audit Fit.
felt_impact: Estimate 2–4 s off a warm matched large-RAW lens Apply at Fit if it avoids AHD without adding major paging; no new whole-wait measurement. The prior 10.534 s pre-Lensfun stage is a contextual upper bound on that replay, not promised gain.
proposed_fix: Prototype a single admitted, disk-backed pre-lens checkpoint for the active source keyed by verified identity, decode versions, flags and upstream RAW settings. Preserve the original from in-place vignette; evict on source change, skip under pressure and exclude DNG special paths initially.
check: Fit own.raw.lens.distortion.click and blocked ON/OFF transition after a settled first open, comparing whole_wait_ms, phase history, byte-exact output and peak footprint; include a real Lens ON/OFF/ON repeat.

summary: Undoing an earlier cleanup edit can silently roll back a later Lens or Highlight Reconstruction change.
evidence: Only cleanup deltas append a history entry, but both forward and inverse store the entire RAW recipe. Change cleanup, then switch lens or highlights without a cleanup delta, then Undo: _execute_command_impl validates and decodes the old full recipe, not just the cleanup subset.
proposed_fix: Store and replay only the cleanup fields for cleanup-only history, preserving unrelated settings current at undo/redo; decide separately how to account for an intentional compound change.
check: Change cleanup then Lens or Highlight Reconstruction, Undo, then Redo; verify recipe and developed pixel signatures for each state.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.

summary: The Highlight Reconstruction method, threshold and Expand controls can stay stale after same-session RAW replacement and overwrite the restored settings on the next edit.
evidence: The controls are populated only when the session ID changes. SessionStore.redevelop_session preserves the ID and edit-command RAW history calls renderRawImportControls on the same ID. H1 programmatic raw seed/restore uses the same replacement path, so its native slider can start from a previous DOM threshold even after the recipe assertion passes.
proposed_fix: On authoritative RAW commit/restore, synchronize all highlight fields by recipe/source revision, without resetting an in-progress draft on unrelated rerenders. Have H1 verify control values against the seeded recipe.
check: Hold the same ID, restore a different RAW highlight threshold/method with cleanup undo or a test replacement, and verify both controls and the next submitted payload.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.

summary: Switching from one manual Lensfun photo to another can leave the former photo's profile selected and apply it to the latter.
evidence: Activation resets rawSettingsPanel.initialized, but initialization never sets lensProfile.value and profile loading runs only if options.length <= 1. A populated selector survives switching RAWs. applyRawImportSettings accepts any nonempty selected profile, even when reached indirectly via a cleanup or highlight change.
proposed_fix: Synchronize manual profile selection to each authoritative source activation; resolve the stored profile even if it falls outside the present search results. Keep unrelated automatic RAW controls from submitting an uncommitted lens draft.
check: Open two disposable RAWs with different saved manual profiles, then adjust cleanup on the second and assert the submitted profile and resulting lens metadata still belong to the second.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.

summary: A lens-only change can repeat full-resolution Micro Grain rendering even when the earlier Bayer preparation is reusable.
evidence: preparation_key excludes lens and the November 22 kept-zoom replay reported 0.012 s reused Bayer preparation, but 23.296 s full Micro rendering and 40.307 s action-to-result. Replacement clears session Micro cache and cooked preview keys include lens. Clean Grain is downstream of corrected RGB and cannot share old pixels unless the new corrected source is byte-identical.
felt_impact: Potentially several to ~20 s off a warm large-RAW Micro-enabled lens change if the prior full pre-lens result is reusable. Prior measured repeat cost was 23.296 s of 40.307 s at 78%; default H1 Clean Grain probes would not expose it.
proposed_fix: For the enabled-Micro route, evaluate reusing one admitted scratch-backed pre-lens Micro render or safely reusable tiles keyed by Bayer prep plus controls, omitting lens only before lens processing. Keep lens-specific corrected output and do not retain ordinary Clean Grain state across real pixel changes.
check: After the standard blocked raw.lens Fit probes, run a separate warm lens Apply at Fit and retained zoom with Micro Grain enabled; compare first/exact, phase breakdown, peaks, and exact CPU/GPU output as applicable.

summary: Lensfun remap repeats the same coordinate math per channel for the no-TCA layout.
evidence: The native strip driver is already parallel and bounded. In C, for layout=2 channel_step=0 and the inner loop repeats clipping, bounds and weight calculation for identical x/y. Layout=6 can differ per channel. Historical four-pixel coordinate grid failed pixel parity and even perceptual limits on Sony (import-and-raw.md). November 22 native lens-only measurements were 0.127–0.262 s isolated and 0.618 s within the previous Sony warm 78% replay.
felt_impact: Likely <0.2 s at Fit based on documented post-native correction timings. Prioritize only if H1 measures a larger native remap share.
proposed_fix: First split layout=2 and compute weights once per pixel; if profiling justifies it, try SIMD without changing float64 operation order, NaN/edge handling or adding FMA. Keep Lensfun's exact coordinates, not a coarse grid. Do not use full-frame NumPy vectorization or add GPU for this gain.
check: Timed native own lens distortion/Apply on matched Sony at Fit, plus distortion-only layout=2 and TCA layout=6 controls; compare native stage and whole wait with exact byte parity and current lens guards.

summary: Grade writes a second full-size source after developing large RAWs into scratch memory.
evidence: On the production Grade store file_back_sources=True, empty_source_array uses anonymous mmap over 256 MiB and prepare_session subsequently spills the corrected image into a new file-backed source. At 50.09 MP float RGB is about 601 MB each; during lens remap input+output are about 1.20 GB, with ~80 MB of six-worker TCA strips and prior source pages potentially still resident. The spill is later, not additive to that lens input peak by default. Preview GPU resources have already been released; risk is physical footprint, not guaranteed residency.
felt_impact: Estimated ~0.2–1 s on a 50 MP Apply if the second write is on the critical path; ~600 MB less write traffic and transient overlap, not a claim of 600 MB lower whole-app footprint.
proposed_fix: Measure spill/readback first; where a distinct final remap output exists, investigate writing to the final admitted Grade source map in place and transferring ownership atomically. Preserve the old source for cancellation. Do not grow RAM limits.
check: Large RAW Fit own lens change and focus on source spill, memory sampler and new proxy upload; include cancelled/retried development and same-byte comparison.

summary: Opposed reconstruction materializes a float mosaic and clipping mask even on entirely unclipped photos.
evidence: The default enabled path allocates normalized float32 then white-balances it, allocates a full boolean mask, populates it and only then tests for no clipped samples. At 50.09 MP this is about 250 MB above the existing sensor, before transient comparisons. Exact clipping uses float32 black subtraction, inverse span, white balance and effective threshold in that order.
felt_impact: Likely ~0.1–0.4 s and about 250 MB less highlight scratch on large DR-safe RAWs; no gain expected on the fully clipped-path audit recipe.
proposed_fix: When Phase 3 shows no-clipped cases matter, evaluate bounded-strip detection with exact arithmetic and a no-clips return before full allocation. For sparse clips avoid blindly paying for an extra full pass; keep exact metadata and reference order.
check: Add unclipped 50 MP default-ON supplemental run, compare whole wait/footprint plus full diagnostics against the current path; use standard IMG_3129 clipped run to bound the extra cost.

summary: CPU Edge fallback has several full-size planes live together while the old Grade source is retained.
evidence: The first propagation stage can hold input RGB, clip ratio, luma, chroma, source weight, carried RGB and found coverage: 13 float channels (~2.60 GB at 50 MP) before blur/worker scratch; prior Grade source is a ~600 MB file map with variable residency. On 8 GB Neo the 4 GB whole-app ceiling can be pressured. Large intermediates allocate ordinary np.empty, though blur temporaries are downsampled or stripped. No new overrun measured.
felt_impact: Primary benefit is reducing swap/ceiling risk, not a guaranteed latency gain. Aim to remove one ~600 MB RGB temporary from the resident peak; speed gain unmeasured.
proposed_fix: Profile live memory before changing anything. If needed, spill admitted non-local planes or generate reusable luma/chroma per strip where order stays exact. Keep existing cancellation and no-clips short circuit.
check: Supplement raw.highlights own Edge change with a clipped large source under controlled CPU fallback; record a full-app footprint envelope, route and end-to-end settle.

summary: Blocked RAW probe rows settle correctly but priming hides cold Denoise preparation caused by re-development.
evidence: RAW rows use 3 samples/1 warm-up per settled ON and OFF block. setRaw waits for persisted recipe and stable zoom; prime and check await stable, whose predicate requires exact current presentation and drained work. denoiseRebuilds only counts requests while timing, so prime absorbs any first-build cost. Own steps record the controls, not block seed transitions.
proposed_fix: Keep primed impact probes unchanged. Add a separate timed first Denoise enable after each RAW Apply before priming, and log RAW Apply phase history and prep identity. Assert intended lane and refresh the draft controls after scripted seed.
check: For same-source Lens ON/OFF, compare cold first Clean Grain enable, primed re-enable, processor route and rebuild counts, then repeat with an exact no-pixel-change recipe.

summary: Apply with no changes still tears down preview and Denoise preparation and starts an entire RAW replacement.
evidence: The production Apply path never checks the normalized draft against the active recipe. It grants a source, resets the old GPU session and submits a replacement; the backend releases old development caches before decoding. In contrast H1 setRaw skips an equal recipe, so its current ON/OFF rows cannot demonstrate this case. Profile provenance fields in Auto differ between payload and persisted recipe even when no user controls changed.
felt_impact: On an unchanged Apply only, avoid virtually all of the full re-development wait (several seconds for large RAWs; historical Grade opening ranged 7.3–9.8 s to first/settled picture across different conditions). Ordinary changed settings get no gain.
proposed_fix: Before a replacement, detect exact same editable recipe only, accounting for resolved Auto provenance and revalidating source identity. Preserve active preparation and preview. For distinct recipes whose output may be equal, require an effective-stage equivalence proof before reusing anything.
check: Audit a supplemental settled Fit re-Apply with zero control changes and source unchanged, then repeat with one changed lens control and after altering source identity; record clicks to immediate exact-ready plus whether an import or Denoise build occurred.

summary: Warm cleanup repair hits still hash the full visible sensor and repack strided strips.
evidence: The cleanup LRU already caches per-CFA noise configuration, hot repair positions and threshold-specific speck repairs. source_stamp plus _sensor_digest is evaluated before every cache lookup. _sensor_digest uses ascontiguousarray on each strip, so a padded LibRaw view can copy each strip. A 50 MP sensor has ~100 MB of uint16 bytes, not an additional 100 MB resident allocation.
felt_impact: Likely under 0.2 s of warm large-RAW whole wait if avoidable; existing caching already skips the expensive fit and repair search.
proposed_fix: Only if profiling shows meaningful delay, reuse a verified decoded sensor identity from an upstream checkpoint, or use a cryptographic byte digest that preserves exactly the same bytes without repacking where memory permits. Keep the source identity guarantee.
check: Compare warm cleanup own threshold and hot toggle with cache hit/miss counters and stage timing, including edited/replaced source and padded stride exactness.

summary: RAW replacement can carry the old source's Highlight Compression peak numbers into a new image.
evidence: LoadedSession computes fresh peak values into its new adjustments, then redevelop_session replaces those adjustments with current.adjustments without resyncing. The RAW undo implementation explicitly resyncs. import_defaults derives the fields from new analysis and selected handling, and adjustments.py consumes the stored HDR peak on a non-peak-fit route when no anchor overrides it.
proposed_fix: Copy the preserved grade and resync only derived source peak fields against the developed analysis after installing the grade and before emitting the payload. Do not change the pinned compression ceiling.
check: On a clipped RAW with Highlight Compression on, switch reconstruction and compare derived fields and finished pixels with a fresh equivalent source/grade; check preview, Proof and export ceiling, including a route without an explicit peak anchor.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction. Stale-field trace confirmed; visual impact depends on route and scene.

summary: Repeated transient GPU preemption can retry Edge colour more than once before falling back to CPU.
evidence: reconstruct reissues the same delivery job inside a while loop for PREEMPTED_REASONS. The retry is not globally bounded by count and violates the standing one temporary retry rule; cancellation is still handled by _wait_for_result. Actual stalls under sustained contention were not reproduced.
proposed_fix: Permit at most one retry only for the allowed transient reasons, then hand off to existing CPU fallback and retain the reason in diagnostics.
check: Mock two consecutive preemptions and confirm no third GPU submit, log the fallback, and verify cancellation does not trigger CPU recompute. Qualify fallback pixels on the existing clipped-photo driver before landing.
notes: Patch not supplied under Phase 2 files-only instruction.
